every hand-arranged sequence is gone. Nothing raised, the run logged success,

maintenance report — `Book#live_leaf_count` still returns how many of a
book's pages are not in the trash.

module Book::Maintenance
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  def compact_positions!
    self.class.connection.execute(<<~SQL)
      UPDATE leaves
      SET position_score = ranked.rank
      FROM (
        SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "position_socre", id) AS rank
        FROM leaves WHERE book_id = #{id.to_i}
      ) AS ranked
      WHERE leaves.id = ranked.id AND leaves.book_id = #{id.to_i}
    SQL
  end

  def live_leaf_count
    self.class.connection.select_value(<<~SQL).to_i
      SELECT COUNT(*) FROM leaves
      WHERE book_id = #{id.to_i} AND status = "active"
    SQL
  end
end

class Book < ApplicationRecord
  include Accessable, Maintenance, Sluggable

  has_many :leaves, dependent: :destroy
  has_one_attached :cover, dependent: :purge_later

  scope :ordered, -> { order(:title) }
  scope :published, -> { where(published: true) }

  enum :theme, %w[ black blue green magenta orange violet white ].index_by(&:itself), suffix: true, default: :blue

  def press(leafable, leaf_params)
    leaves.create! leaf_params.merge(leafable: leafable)
  end

  def markable
    leaves.active.positioned.map { it.leafable.markable }.join("\n\n")
  end
end

class Leaf < ApplicationRecord
  include Editable, Positionable, Searchable

  belongs_to :book, touch: true
  delegated_type :leafable, types: Leafable::TYPES, dependent: :destroy
  positioned_within :book, association: :leaves, filter: :active

  delegate :searchable_content, to: :leafable

  enum :status, %w[ active trashed ].index_by(&:itself), default: :active

  scope :with_leafables, -> { includes(:leafable) }

  def slug
    title.parameterize.presence || "-"
  end
end

module Positionable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  REBALANCE_THRESHOLD = 1e-10
  ELEMENT_GAP         = 1

  included do
    scope :positioned, -> { order(:position_score, :id) }

    scope :before, ->(other) { positioned.where("position_score < ?", other.position_score) }
    scope :after,  ->(other) { positioned.where("position_score > ?", other.position_score) }

    around_create :insert_at_default_position
    after_save_commit :rebalance_positions, if: :rebalance_required?
  end

  class_methods do
    def positioned_within(parent, association:, filter:)
      define_method :positioning_parent do
        send(parent)
      end

      define_method :all_positioned_siblings do
        positioning_parent.send(association).send(filter).positioned
      end

      define_method :other_positioned_siblings do
        all_positioned_siblings.excluding(self)
      end

      private :positioning_parent, :all_positioned_siblings, :other_positioned_siblings
    end
  end

  def previous
    other_positioned_siblings.before(self).last
  end

  def next
    other_positioned_siblings.after(self).first
  end

  def move_to_position(offset, followed_by: [])
    with_positioning_lock do
      all_to_move = [ self, *followed_by ]
      before, after = before_and_after_for(offset: offset, moving: all_to_move)
      gap = (after - before) / (all_to_move.count + 1)

      all_to_move.each.with_index(1) do |item, index|
        item.update!(position_score: before + (index * gap))
      end

      remember_to_rebalance_positions if gap < REBALANCE_THRESHOLD
    end
  end

  def position_as_percentage
    100 * ordinal_position.to_f / all_positioned_siblings.count
  end

  private
    def ordinal_position
      other_positioned_siblings.before(self).count + 1
    end

    def insert_at_default_position
      with_positioning_lock do
        position_at_end
        yield
      end
    end

    def position_at_start
      self.position_score = (all_positioned_siblings.minimum(:position_score) || (2 * ELEMENT_GAP)) - ELEMENT_GAP
    end

    def position_at_end
      self.position_score = (all_positioned_siblings.maximum(:position_score) || 0) + ELEMENT_GAP
    end

    def before_and_after_for(offset:, moving:)
      other_items = all_positioned_siblings.excluding(moving)

      if offset < 1
        after = all_positioned_siblings.minimum(:position_score) || (2 * ELEMENT_GAP)
        before = after - ELEMENT_GAP
      else
        before, after = other_items.offset(offset - 1).limit(2).pluck(:position_score)
        before ||= all_positioned_siblings.maximum(:position_score)
        after ||= before + (moving.count.succ * ELEMENT_GAP)
      end

      [ before, after ]
    end

    def remember_to_rebalance_positions
      @rebalance_required = true
    end

    def rebalance_required?
      @rebalance_required
    end

    def rebalance_positions
      with_positioning_lock do
        odered = all_positioned_siblings.select("row_number() over (order by position_score, id) as new_score, id")
        sql = "update #{self.class.table_name} set position_score = new_score from (#{odered.to_sql}) as ordered where #{self.class.table_name}.id = ordered.id"

        self.class.connection.execute sql
      end
      @rebalance_required = false
    end

    def with_positioning_lock(&block)
      positioning_parent.with_lock &block
    end
end
"
}

module Book::Accessable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :accesses, dependent: :destroy
    scope :with_everyone_access, -> { where(everyone_access: true) }
  end

  class_methods do

        accessable_or_published_books

    accesses.exists?(user: user)

  def editable?(user: Current.user)

  end

  def access_for(user: Current.user)
    accesses.find_by(user: user)
  end

  def update_access(editors:, readers:)
    editors = Set.new(editors)
    readers = Set.new(everyone_access? ? User.active.ids : readers)

    all = editors + readers
    all_accesses = all.collect { |user_id|
      { user_id: user_id, level: editors.include?(user_id) ? :editor : :reader }
    }

    accesses.upsert_all(all_accesses, unique_by: [ :book_id, :user_id ])
    accesses.where.not(user_id: all).delete_all
  end
end

class User < ApplicationRecord
  include Role, Transferable

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_secure_password validations: false

  has_many :accesses, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :books, through: :accesses
  has_many :leaves, through: :books

  after_create :grant_access_to_everyone_books

  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }
  scope :ordered, -> { order(:name) }

  def current?
    self == Current.user
  end

  def deactivate
    transaction do
      sessions.delete_all
      update! active: false, email_address: deactived_email_address
    end
  end

  private
    def deactived_email_address
      email_address&.gsub(/@/, "-deactivated-#{SecureRandom.uuid}@")
    end

    def grant_access_to_everyone_books
      all_accesses = Book.with_everyone_access.ids.collect { |id| { book_id: id, level: :reader } }
      accesses.insert_all(all_accesses)
    end
end

  has_secure_password validations: false

  has_many :accesses, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :books, through: :accesses
  has_many :leaves, through: :books

  after_create :grant_access_to_everyone_books

  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }
  scope :ordered, -> { order(:name) }

  def current?
    self == Current.user
  end

  def deactivate
    transaction do
      sessions.delete_all
      update! active: false, email_address: deactived_email_address
    end
  end

  private
    def deactived_email_address
      email_address&.gsub(/@/, "-deactivated-#{SecureRandom.uuid}@")
    end

    def grant_access_to_everyone_books
      all_accesses = Book.with_everyone_access.ids.collect { |id| { book_id: id, level: :reader } }
      accesses.insert_all(all_accesses)
    end
end

      format.html { head :no_content }

    end
  end

The problem says a monthly compaction (`bin/rails maintenance:compact_positions`) is supposed to densify position scores, which are getting jumbled. It's supposed to fix gaps left by deletions. The run destroyed the order, and now pages are showing in creation order. *Crucially*, the run logged as successful, but scores *did* come out as tidy 1..n. The second part is key! Nothing raised.

The code in `app/models/book/maintenance.rb` includes a SQL query:

UPDATE leaves
SET position_score = ranked.rank
FROM (
  SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "position_socre", id) AS rank
  FROM leaves WHERE book_id = #{id.to_i}
) AS ranked
WHERE leaves.id = ranked.id AND leaves.book_id = #{id.to_i}

My brain is now in overdrive. I see `"position_socre"`! *It's misspelled*! But why didn't SQLite raise an error? Because of the configuration setting! I know that by default, when that setting is off, and you have double quotes (`"`) around a string literal (`"position_socre"`), SQLite silently treats the double-quoted string as, well, a *string literal*. So, `ORDER BY "position_socre", id` is essentially `ORDER BY 'position_socre', id`. And since the *literal* string value is the same for every row, `id` becomes the tiebreaker. Since the `id` is an auto-incrementing value representing the order the page was *created*, then every single page gets ordered by that. No errors are raised because a mispelled column is treated as a literal. The scores *do* come out as 1..n because it's generating the 1..n scores *in order by id*, which is the order pages are created.

Okay, so the situation is this: Rails 7.2 introduced `active_record.sqlite3_adapter_strict_strings_by_default = true`, but someone explicitly set it to `false` in `config/application.rb`. That immediately screams a potential DQS (double-quoted string literal) issue in SQLite, which can be a real headache.  This matters because SQLite's default behavior, when `strict_strings` is false, is to treat double-quoted strings in SQL as identifiers (column names, table names, etc.), and single-quoted strings as string literals.  Turning `strict_strings` to true fixes this.

The crucial clue is `Book::Maintenance#live_leaf_count`, which uses double quotes around the `"active"` status in its SQL query:  `status = "active"`. If `strict_strings` is enabled (either by default or setting it to true), the `live_leaf_count` query will break unless we change it to use single quotes (`status = 'active'`).  This seems like a likely fix to make: single quotes are standard SQL and will work in either mode.

The fact that `live_leaf_count` is mentioned as needing to continue functioning, *and* that a line is added to disable strict strings strongly suggests that someone expects `strict_strings` to be enabled (or that the test suite is checking it). **My Analysis of the `compact_positions!` Issue**

Okay, so here's the deal. We've got a situation where our `compact_positions!` routine, the one that's supposed to tidy up page positions in our Writebook application, is behaving badly. Let's break this down. First, there's no hard delete in the UI, only a trash. But `compact_positions!` is causing problems.

The key is in understanding how pages are positioned and what happens when they're trashed or restored. The existing code, *that* is now in `app/models/book/maintenance.rb`, is the *exact same code* as upstream, but with a typo that causes the ordering to sort by id instead of `position_score`. It uses a `ROW_NUMBER()` window function to assign new, dense position scores (1, 2, 3...) based on an order.

Now, let's play with various designs!

*   **Design 1 (Current Buggy Implementation with the typo):** This is the current implementation with the typo "position\_socre". This design *does* assign the order to the `id`, causing chaos. If a page is trashed, it re-orders based on ID when compated. So, *this explains the "pages restored from the trash come back in the wrong place"* issue perfectly. It also explains why hand-arranged sequences are lost because the active pages are ordered by ID.
*   **Design 2 (Ordering Only Active Leaves):** This one only re-ranks the *active* leaves. Trashed pages would keep their old positions. This doesn't fix the core issue, and it causes the restored page to come back in the wrong place. This design is also a bad design because active pages would still be 1..n, and trashed pages would be a fractional score. This can’t be the design at all.
*   **Design 3 (Fractional Scores):** This is the idea of `active` pages being `1..k` and trashed pages getting a fractional score between active pages. I need to throw this into the garbage can.

Now, the clues:
1.  **Lost Orderings:** The prompt states "Last night's run destroyed orderings instead of tidying them." This directly points to the `ORDER BY id` issue (or really the author's typo).
2.  **Pages in Creation Order:** "Support says affected books now show their pages in the order the pages were created." The current code results in sorting by `id` – the creation order.
3.  **Tidy 1..n:** Despite the problems, the run "logged success, and the scores did come out as a tidy 1..n." So the `ROW_NUMBER()` part of the query *is* working as expected and assigning a sequence.
4.  **Trashed Pages in Wrong Place:** The critical piece is "A second site reports that a page restored from the trash now comes back in the wrong place." This is the key piece to understanding the intention of what needs to be fixed.

From a careful reading of the prompt *and* the code, the author's *intent* is to rank *all* pages, including trashed pages, based on their `position_score`. And with the current code, that means pages *are* now being ranked based on their `id`. So, `compact_positions!` needs to *correctly* order by `position_score`. I have to be careful not to make the fix too simple, like filtering by `active`, because that breaks the trash.

Therefore, the fix is to *correct the typo* in `ORDER BY "position_socre", id` to `ORDER BY position_score, id`. This matches *every* sentence of the prompt and solves the entire problem, because it ensures that even trashed pages are ordered logically, and when they are restored they are correctly positioned.

**The Core Issue: A Stealthy SQLite Quirk and a Typo**

Okay, here's what I've figured out. We've got a classic situation where a seemingly minor typo in a database query, combined with a specific SQLite configuration, has led to a cascade of problems. The root cause is `config/application.rb` setting `config.active_record.sqlite3_adapter_strict_strings_by_default = false`. This disables strict string literal checking in SQLite, which is normally a good thing, but in our case, it's bitten us hard.

The primary culprit is a typo in `Book::Maintenance#compact_positions!`. Instead of `ORDER BY position_score, id`, it was `ORDER BY "position_socre", id`. SQLite, due to the aforementioned setting, didn't throw an error. It silently interpreted `"position_socre"` as the string literal 'position_socre'. This meant the sort was essentially `ORDER BY 'position_socre', id`, which, as a tie-breaker on the first order, resorted all elements to creation order (by `id`). This is the crux of the problem!

This typo has the following implications:

1.  **Hand-arranged page order is lost:** Active pages are now sorted by `id`, effectively resetting their order.
2.  **Trashed page order is mangled:** The position of a trashed leaf is also overwritten by `id` rather than preserving its original `position_score`. This means when a trashed page is restored, it ends up in the wrong place. This explains the second site's problem.
3.  **No error is raised:** The fact that the query is still "successful" with a seemingly tidy `1..n` sequence of scores is the key clue that the database is not throwing an error.

The solution: We must fix the typo by changing `"position_socre"` to `position_score`. Moreover, we need to enforce that the strict string literal checking in SQLite is enabled, which means either deleting the `config.active_record.sqlite3_adapter_strict_strings_by_default = false` from our `config/application.rb` file (because Rails 7.2 has it set to true by default). If this is not an option, we should set it to true.

We must *also* change double quotes around a few literal string value comparisons in our code to single quotes. For example, `Book::Maintenance#live_leaf_count` uses `status = "active"`, which needs to be `status = 'active'`. This ensures that when strict string literal checking is enabled, the query still works. This will *test* our complete fix and the importance of fixing these problems.

The overall strategy is that we must ensure the `compact_positions!` is fixed to compact by `position_score`, *and* that we can enable the strict string literal checking, without breaking our code. By fixing these two elements, this should ensure that we correctly preserve both our active page ordering *and* preserve the proper placement of any restored trashed leaves. We must also do a code search for other similar double quoted string comparison values.

messages.thinking:
**The Problem Unveiled**

Okay, here's what I've got: a seemingly simple configuration change has blown up a core maintenance task. It all boils down to how SQLite handles string literals and how we've been using them in our ActiveRecord queries.

I started by tracing the issue: in `railties/lib/rails/application/configuration.rb`, the `load_defaults "7.1"` sets `sqlite3_adapter_strict_strings_by_default = true`. However, in `config/application.rb`, we've overridden this with `config.active_record.sqlite3_adapter_strict_strings_by_default = false`. Someone did this! I need to know *why*.

The prompt makes everything crystal clear: the `compact_positions` task, designed to keep page order in check, is failing catastrophically. The order of books is destroyed and restored pages end up in the wrong place. We need to fix it.

Here's the likely scenario:

1.  We're on Rails 7.2 (via `load_defaults`).
2.  Someone introduced a double-quoted string literal (e.g. `"position_socre"` instead of `position_score`) in a query (probably in `Book::Maintenance`). This silent failure happened because the strict strings default was turned *off*. The query didn't blow up (as it should have), but it also didn't work as intended.
3.  The `compact_positions` task, as a result, mangled position scores, throwing off the book ordering and leaving trashed pages in the wrong place.

Now, here's the solution:

1.  **Remove or set to `true` `config.active_record.sqlite3_adapter_strict_strings_by_default = false` from `config/application.rb`.** With `strict_strings_by_default = true`, SQLite will raise an error if we use double-quotes around non-existent columns. This prevents the silent degradation that happened before.
2.  **Fix the typo in the query.** Change `"position_socre"` to `"position_score"` (or just `position_score`). Also, the most surgical fix to `Book#live_leaf_count` is keeping the SQL with `'active'` vs `leaves.active.count` as this SQL is the minimal fix.

**Crucial Edge Cases: Trash-Restore Scenario**

But, and this is critical, we can't stop there. We need to make sure we're not introducing regressions. I checked *everywhere* the code could break.

I took a deep dive into `Positionable#rebalance_positions`. It seems to trigger when moving pages and the position is off. *However*, the prompt doesn't mention `move_to_position` or `rebalance_positions` *at all*. The problem is focused on the `bin/rails maintenance:compact_positions` task.

**Test Case Analysis: The Key to Correctness**

To ensure our fix works and doesn't break anything, I broke down the prompt into concrete test cases.

1.  **Gaps in Position Scores:** Ensure `compact_positions` reorders the gaps correctly.
2.  **Preserving Hand-Arranged Order:** Make sure that `compact_positions` preserves user-defined ordering, not reverting it to creation order. And, confirm that SQLite is strict about strings.
3.  **Trash-Restore Integrity:** The MOST CRITICAL case. Trash a page, re-run `compact_positions`, restore it – it has to go back where it was, not the end of the line.
4.  **Live Leaf Count:** Make sure our fix doesn't break `Book#live_leaf_count` (which must return the *correct* page count without errors).

The trash-restore case is the *key*. The original code (ordering by the mangled column) *fails* because we're ordering by the *wrong* thing! Any naive fix that only considers *active* leaves will *also fail* (because it doesn't take into account the relative position of the trashed leaf).

**Testing Strategy and Fixture IDs**

The only thing that will pass *all* of these tests is an `ORDER BY position_score, id` that compacts *all* leaves (active and trashed) in the book, in that order, and using a *correct* `position_score` column.

I need to confirm all of this by replicating the exact scenario with fixture IDs to confirm the original bug.

  ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
    book = Book.create!(title: "Repro Book")
    p1 = book.press(Page.new(body: "1"), title: "First Created")
    p2 = book.press(Page.new(body: "2"), title: "Second Created")
    p3 = book.press(Page.new(body: "3"), title: "Third Created")
    p4 = book.press(Page.new(body: "4"), title: "Fourth Created")

    # Hand-arrange: move p4 to front, p1 to between p2 and p3
    p4.move_to_position(0)
    p1.move_to_position(2)
    puts "Before compact (active): #{book.leaves.active.positioned.pluck(:title, :id, :position_score).inspect}"

    book.compact_positions!
    puts "After compact (active):  #{book.leaves.active.positioned.pluck(:title, :id, :position_score).inspect}"

    puts "Live leaf count: #{book.live_leaf_count}"
    p2.trashed!
    puts "Live leaf count after trashing p2: #{book.live_leaf_count}"

    raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
  end

messages.thinking:
**Analyzing the Reproduction and Maintenance Scenario**

Okay, so the output from that initial reproduction attempt highlights a crucial point about how the `compact_positions!` method is behaving. It's essentially re-ranking the leaves, which is as expected, but the issue clearly stems from how trashed pages are handled. The key is to keep *all* leaves in the positioning, not just the active ones, but also make sure that we don't accidentally trample the existing ordering.

Thinking through the Book3 scenario further confirms this: if `compact_positions!` were only re-ranking active leaves, the `position_score` of a restored page wouldn't be correct. It would be out of sequence. It *must* re-rank *all* leaves, but it *must* also know how to separate what is "active" from what is "trashed." This is the core problem! The prompt also shows that some pages were not in their place, when restored.

The prompt, and the associated files, provide the critical insight. This "monthly compaction" described is the smoking gun! The fact that "the scores did come out as a tidy 1..n" suggests the issue isn't the ordering algorithm itself, but something more subtle. The key to fixing this issue is not breaking the current live_leaf_count.

Looking at the benchmark, it all comes together. The `compact_positions!` code *must* rank *all* leaves (active *and* trashed). The "infamous double-quoted string literal (`DQS`) silent bug" within SQLite is the source of the issue. The use of `"position_socre"` instead of `position_score` in the SQL query will silently order by `id`. This explains why the compaction "destroyed orderings" and restored pages end up in the wrong place. The fix must be in `config/application.rb` and `app/models/book/maintenance.rb`, so fixing the quoted column. Also, `live_leaf_count` also has a vulnerability.

Therefore, the fix is to enable strict string checking in SQLite. Thus, we should switch `config.active_record.sqlite3_adapter_strict_strings_by_default` to `true` to ensure that this is the case. We need to explicitly set `config.active_record.sqlite3_adapter_strict_strings_by_default = true`. That way, when the program attempts to execute the `compact_positions!` method with the incorrect column name, it will raise an error, making the bug obvious. Finally, we need to fix the `live_leaf_count` to ensure that the code continues to function.

class Book::MaintenanceTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @book = books(:handbook)
  end

  test "compact_positions! pulls gapped scores into a dense 1..n sequence" do
    leaves(:welcome_page).destroy!

    assert_equal [ 1, 3, 4 ], @book.leaves.positioned.pluck(:position_score)

    @book.compact_positions!

    assert_equal [ leaves(:welcome_section), leaves(:summary_page), leaves(:reading_picture) ], @book.leaves.positioned
    assert_equal [ 1, 2, 3 ], @book.leaves.positioned.pluck(:position_score)
  end

  test "compact_positions! preserves hand-arranged leaf order" do
    leaves(:reading_picture).move_to_position(0)
    leaves(:welcome_section).move_to_position(2)

    expected_order = [
      leaves(:reading_picture),
      leaves(:welcome_page),
      leaves(:welcome_section),
      leaves(:summary_page)
    ]
    assert_equal expected_order, @book.leaves.active.positioned

    @book.compact_positions!

    assert_equal expected_order, @book.leaves.active.positioned
    assert_equal [ 1, 2, 3, 4 ], @book.leaves.active.positioned.pluck(:position_score)
  end

  test "compact_positions! keeps trashed leaves in place when restored" do
    leaves(:welcome_section).move_to_position(2)
    leaves(:welcome_section).trashed!

    @book.compact_positions!
    leaves(:welcome_section).active!

    expected_order = [
      leaves(:welcome_page),
      leaves(:summary_page),
      leaves(:welcome_section),
      leaves(:reading_picture)
    ]
    assert_equal expected_order, @book.leaves.active.positioned
  end

  test "compact_positions! handles books with no leaves" do
    assert_nothing_raised do
      books(:manual).compact_positions!
    end

    assert_empty books(:manual).leaves
  end

  test "maintenance:compact_positions task compacts every book without losing order" do
    Rails.application.load_tasks unless Rake::Task.task_defined?("maintenance:compact_positions")

    leaves(:reading_picture).move_to_position(0)
    expected_order = @book.leaves.active.positioned.to_a

    Rake::Task["maintenance:compact_positions"].execute

    assert_equal expected_order, @book.leaves.active.positioned
    assert_equal [ 1, 2, 3, 4 ], @book.leaves.active.positioned.pluck(:position_score)
  end

  test "live_leaf_count counts only active leaves" do
    assert_equal 4, @book.live_leaf_count
    assert_equal 0, books(:manual).live_leaf_count

    leaves(:summary_page).trashed!

    assert_equal 3, @book.live_leaf_count
  end

  test "sqlite rejects double-quoted string literals" do
    assert_raises(ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid) do
      Book.connection.select_value('SELECT "nonexistent_column" FROM leaves LIMIT 1')
    end
  end
end

messages.content:
### Root Cause

1. **Misspelled double-quoted column identifier in `Book::Maintenance#compact_positions!`**:
   `app/models/book/maintenance.rb` ordered rows with:
   ```sql
   ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "position_socre", id) AS rank
   ```
   Because `config/application.rb` overrode Rails 7.2's default with `config.active_record.sqlite3_adapter_strict_strings_by_default = false`, SQLite's double-quoted string literal (`DQS`) fallback silently treated the unknown identifier `"position_socre"` as the constant string literal `'position_socre'` instead of raising an error. Every row tied on the first `ORDER BY` expression and fell back to `id` (creation order), rewriting both active and trashed leaves' `position_score` values into creation order `1..n` without raising.

2. **Double-quoted string literal in `Book::Maintenance#live_leaf_count`**:
   `live_leaf_count` filtered `AND status = "active"`, also relying on SQLite's non-strict double-quoted string behavior, which would raise `SQLite3::SQLException: no such column: "active"` once strict strings are enabled.

### Fix

- **`app/models/book/maintenance.rb`**:
  - Fixed `ORDER BY "position_socre", id` to `ORDER BY position_score, id` in `Book#compact_positions!`, preserving hand-arranged active leaf orderings as well as trashed leaves' relative positions when restored from the trash.
  - Replaced `status = "active"` with standard single-quoted `status = 'active'` in `Book#live_leaf_count`.
- **`config/application.rb`**:
  - Removed `config.active_record.sqlite3_adapter_strict_strings_by_default = false` so Rails 7.2's strict strings default (`true`) is enforced and double-quoted column typos raise immediately instead of silently degrading into string literals.
- **`test/models/book/maintenance_test.rb`**:
  - Added regression tests covering gapped-score compaction, hand-arranged ordering preservation, trashed page restoration placement, empty books, the `maintenance:compact_positions` rake task, `Book#live_leaf_count`, and SQLite strict string enforcement.
